open_items: docs/website-rebuild/verification-summary.json is historical evidence from arena/ad9fd719-cloudhost247 and must not be read as current-branch evidence.
The published documentation set includes docs/NODE_PLATFORM_STATUS.md, which references internal pull-request state; decide whether it stays public.

The PHP sitemap entry points (cloudhost247-sitemap.php, tools-sitemap.php, builder-sitemap.php) still build their own lists; they have not yet been pointed at the registry policy the Node sitemap now enforces.
scripts/generate-global-platform.py still maintains the legacy tools-public.json category set; it is accepted as a secondary source but should be retired once nothing reads it.
The far larger rebuild brief (per-page PHP visual regeneration, the 3D illustration system, browser-level responsive/a11y QA) is not part of this changeset.
findings_fixed: Nine of the ten tool-category links published by the header and footer pointed at slugs no engine could resolve (the registry carried the legacy PHP engine's slugs, while the theme runtime and the React Tools Center both serve the discovery categories). The registry now publishes dns-domains, ip-network, security, ssl, email, website, developer, calculators and utilities, and a new Node test pins every published category to a non-empty catalogue category.

The Tools mega menu published zero links on the PHP surface (empty groups) and the PHP integration suite failed on it; the menu now publishes the nine server-rendered category floors, and the suite validates all of them.
The MRZ tool - a registered, public, browser-only tool - was missing from the PHP footer Tools column. It is now published with the agreed label.

The generator and scripts/verify-website.py validated PHP tool destinations against the legacy tools-public.json only; both now accept the authoritative theme projection tools.json (the file the PHP runtime reads) as well.
The PHP website suite asserted 'all seven mega menu categories'; it now pins the nine published families by id, matching the SPA.
